questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very straightforward, and they send you plenty of information. One thing to note: if you are unable to attend the welcome days and instead have a welcome meeting, which they will invite you to, I would recommend asking them to send you information on how to log in to the university's online learning portal before the semester starts. That way, you'll be ready from the first day of classes.

questions.answer: There were dedicated welcome days organized for incoming students, as well as a welcome meeting for those who were unable to attend. In general, they take very good care of international students and have very friendly staff whose sole responsibility is to support and assist us

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: "It's great to be able to walk to campus, so in that respect living in Saldanha is ideal. However, it is also a bit far from many of the city's other attractions and social areas. questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Fenix+ is also where you register for courses. Course enrollment is on a first-come, first-served basis, so make sure you are ready on the day registration opens. You can browse the available courses on the ISCTE website, where you can also view the different class sections and schedules by clicking on each course.

When it is time to register, I recommend having a prioritized list of courses and preferred time slots prepared in advance, so you can enroll quickly before the classes fill up.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching style is very different from what I was used to. There is significantly less reading, as most of the material is recommended rather than required. Active participation in class is expected, and there is a strong emphasis on group work/ group presentations.

I also found that lecturers interacted with students quite differently. In my experience, when students challenged a point or engaged in the discussions that lecturers themselves encouraged, some lecturers would occasionally laugh at or react dismissively to students' comments. I found this to be somewhat condescending and discouraging. Compared to Danish standards, the teaching approach felt more hierarchical and, at times, less pedagogically supportive.

questions.answer: I would recommend taking courses in Political Science, as they have a good structure and competent lecturers. I would avoid Sociology and the Business School in general. I would recommend ‘Portuguese History and Culture’ if you are able to get it approved for credit—it is interesting to learn about Portugal, and the lecturer is very kind, engaging, and fun

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I most appreciated the welcoming and supportive approach towards international students, as well as the generally friendly and informal atmosphere. This made it easy to settle in and meet new people. I also really valued the opportunity to experience Portuguese culture and lifestyle outside of university.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
First, be prepared for a different academic culture. The teaching style is more based on participation and group work, and there is generally less mandatory reading and a different level of academic depth compared to UCPH. It takes some adjustment, so go in with an open mind.

Second, make sure you are ready for course registration as soon as it opens. It is first-come, first-served, and popular classes fill up quickly. Have a clear list of preferred courses and time slots in advance.

Third, take advantage of your time outside of university. Travel around the country, meet other students, and experience the local culture.
